No phonology; notes only villagers born before ca. 1940 speak it; cites Ethnologue 25, PARADISEC DL2 and WF3.

sources.citation: Sanders, Arden G. & Joy Sanders. 1980. Defining the centres of the Marienberg language family. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 20, Pacific Linguistics A-56: 171-196.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistics (Mandi 41% with Muniwara, 25% average cognates) and sociolinguistic/schooling notes (sec. 5.2.6 Mandi); no phonology.

sources.citation: Sanders, Joy & Arden G. Sanders. 1980. Dialect survey of the Kamasau language. Pacific Linguistics A-56: 137-170.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing relevant: covers Kamasau villages only; Mandi/Wiarumus not mentioned; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 767-780. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.769 phylum-level phonological characterisation (three places of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, high proportion of fricatives) makes no mention of stress; Mandi is named only as a Marienberg language apparently lacking gender (p.772) and in the family list.
